chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who marries a woman and consummates the marriage, then she claims her dowry from him.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has entered upon her, he has paid the immediate portion (of the dowry).'

Therefore, there is nothing in any of these narrations that contradicts what we mentioned, because all of them include that the woman claims the dowry. And we did not say that she is given the dowry merely by her claim; rather, she needs evidence. And when there is no evidence with her other than her claim, she has nothing, according to what these narrations include. And only the full payment of her dowry is required after the evidence is established for her.
And that which indicates that evidence is required from her is what he narrated:

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: Consummated the marriage / Entered upon her
key_terms.هَدَمَ الْعَاجِلَ: Paid the immediate portion (idiom for fulfilling the due part)

ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for a wife to claim her dowry in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal distinction between the obligation to pay the immediate dowry upon consummation and the evidentiary burden required to claim it. It reinforces the Shia jurisprudential principle that a wife’s mere assertion is insufficient for payment; she must provide valid proof (bayyinah), ensuring that the husband’s liability is confirmed through evidence rather than unilateral claim.
